[quote]或许每个人都思索过同一个问题——“人死后会去往哪里？” 《Dice With Death》告诉我们，人死后会被死神拉着玩骰子。[/quote] [h2] 继续梭哈？还是及时收手？[/h2] 游戏的玩法机制有点像Farkle，融合了肉鸽游戏和卡牌游戏的构筑元素。游戏的玩法很简单，每回合投掷骰子，然后从投掷出的骰子中选择组合得分并存入银行。接着玩家可以选择结束回合对死神造成银行得分的伤害，或者选择继续掷骰子以获取更高的分数。但如果运气不好，没有得分组合的话，就会触发失误，导致之前存入银行的所有分数丢失。什么？你问我是继续梭哈还是及时收手？像我这种赌怪，我肯定选择梭哈啦~~ 游戏后面还会解锁各式各样、效果独特的骰子和遗物，使得每次掷骰子和构筑的策略都变得越来越复杂，玩法也更加多样化。目前游戏还有战士和治疗师两种职业可供选择，它们各自拥有不同的游戏机制。 死神不仅仅是你的对手。每当你打败他，他会与你对话，分享一些故事，赠送你一些独特的骰子和遗物，以此来推进游戏进程。 [h2]阴郁的氛围感[/h2] 游戏的画面氛围很有味道，用简单的像素风成功营造出一种阴郁的氛围感。 [h2]一些遗憾[/h2] 作为一款抢先体验游戏，《Dice With Death》免不了存在一些可以改进之处。目前游戏没有中文，也没有成就系统。还有就是有时游戏会出现大量数值叠加的情况，但因缺乏详细的步骤记录，我经常来不及反应这些数值是如何叠加的。 [h2]总结[/h2] 一款令人上瘾的骰子构筑肉鸽游戏，它将Farkle式的风险与回报机制与丰富的策略构筑巧妙融合。简单的像素风成功营造出一种阴郁的氛围感，令人沉浸其中。不过目前游戏尚处于抢先体验阶段，内容量有待扩充，缺乏中文支持，但其核心玩法扎实，潜力巨大。若你喜欢这种策略性构筑与高风险博弈的乐趣，《Dice With Death》绝对值得一试！ [quote] 恭请雅鉴 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

TL;DR: Once Second Circle hits, you have absolutely no wiggle room to breathe and hit the cool combos that you experience in base difficulty. Which takes away a huge portion of fun for the game, since you just have to constantly restart to just get past the few stages without having Death upgrading its dice, so you never get to see your build truly "come online". Unfortunately, the balance goes entirely out the window once you reach Second Circle, where you basically need to immediately win within 3 rounds or else Death rapidly outscales you with consistent 100+ damage attacks. This means you really only have one strategy: to take maximum-DPS relics ASAP. This gets extremely tiresome when you only get to pick from around 8 common dice at the start, one of which is utterly useless (Razor's Edge, which has a 33% chance to do 5 damage... or 1.8% of Death's HP in the very first round). Obviously some level of RNG is to be expected, but it feels like the amount of truly winnable games is already <10% once you reach Second Circle. The other annoying thing is that the coolest, rarest dice (Alpha Dice, Dice of Many Faces, King's Guard, etc.) appear to be locked after winning a certain number of rounds. This means that - barring the first time you unlock one of those rare dice (that you can then instantly use *for that run*) - you'll never see it again in 90% of your Second Circle runs (except for the Pickaxe, and even then it's only active for one round).

I unlocked and played all characters in 6 hours, enough to feel done with what the game has to offer in it's current state. As mentioned in other reviews, death gets a little crazy in higher levels with extra dice, allowing perfect rolls every time. The game could use some balancing, more characters, and maybe add a limited 're-roll dice' option, or something, to give user a bit more agency in a terrible run of luck. Overall Dice with Death has solid bones. I look forward to re-playing after official release. Also, I like the idea of character game-play diversity, but playing the witch just felt too random. I just rolled, and stuff happened, this could perhaps be fixed by better explanation of the spell dynamics, but coming in blind, the character just didn't click. Look at 'Dice & Fold' for guidance, that game has a huge list of characters/modifiers, but each feels well crafted, and engaging. I absolutely see this game being as deep and re-playable eventually, but it needs some additional well crafted content to get there.

I refunded the game because the Witch character doesn't work. That's entirely it. The Witch is a character that you unlock after defeating Death at the second difficult level. The problem is that the Witch doesn't work like the other classes. With other characters you're always doing damage just by scoring runs (single pair, double pair, straight, etc, etc), but the Witch powers "spells" by rolling specific die numbers. Runs for the Witch do no damage at all. To deal damage you have to use these spells. The basic damage spell requires a 1, 2, and 3 die face. This is quite difficult to get off consistently, especially when failing to score a run (even though runs do literally nothing for the Witch) removes die faces from your spells. The Witch has other spells, but they all require a ton of [i]specific[/i] die faces to actually cast, with most being pretty worthless. Her "ultimate" spell (and I say ultimate as it requires the most die faces) is Wild Magic. Wild Magic is garbage. Sure, it could do 80 damage (forget the fact that it took three turns to get the die faces to cast it, and by that point other classes would have easily pinged for 200 damage), or it could increase your run score by 10! You know, the run score that the Witch literally sees no benefit from! Woo HOO! LET'S GO! I tried to get the Witch to work, but I couldn't get past the first round. Not the first [b]DIFFICULTY[/b]- the FIRST ROUND of the first difficulty. This is after I had literally sailed through the first and second difficulties as the healer without even needing to use their little cauldron gimmick. The Witch is busted and unplayable- and if one out of four of your classes doesn't even function, why am I even playing your game? Maybe the class does actually work. Maybe this is a skill issue thing. There are subclasses for the Witch. The problem is that when I unlocked the Witch, literally my second run in the game, I hadn't unlocked any of the relics the Witch could use. So, I was just raw dogging the Witch without any subclass that might have helped out. [b]BUT HERE'S THE THING[/b] if the Witch class doesn't function without specific relics- why aren't they immediately unlocked the moment you unlock the Witch?! Why do I need to play another boring run as the Healer or Soldier in the [i]hope[/i] that Death bores me with yet another insipid diatribe on the state of existence that ends up producing a Witch relic? There is a fourth class- the Adventurer. I did unlock it, but it also has no subclasses available until you find the right relic. And I didn't want to get into another Witch situation, so I opted for a refund and a negative review. If you like Yahtzee with Death, this might be the game for you. I found it rather boring and fundamentally broken. ALSO, the game is like 3GB in size?!! Like, Slay the Spire 2 only needs 2.5GB and has a ton more art assets. What unoptimized nonsense is this.

I want to like this game, but there's so much wasted potential here on top of just being way too RNG dependent for me. I literally cannot beat the second tier of difficulty and I've tried over 5 times now. Just had my closest run yet and Death did over 200 damage two turns in a row and wiped me out right at the finish line. I'd honestly forgive the game being "hard" if there weren't so many confusing descriptions in this game coupled with a lack of visual appeal. Mild example: Whenever you trigger the perfect dice bank, respawn an extra base dice that lasts until the end of your turn. If you have less than three, also restore a Relic Reroll between rounds. Three what? I assume it means Relic Rerolls, but the first half talks about dice. Worst example: If your initial roll contains four or less dice, reinforce 1. If it contained 1, reinforce 2 instead. Excuse me what? Your initial roll MUST CONTAIN six dice, that's how the game is played. What on earth are they even talking about here? IF IT CONTAINED 1???? What???? I genuinely think you aren't using the word initial right. I get that this is an English as second language game, but games like this are defined by the player knowing wtf is going on. Game's already super RNG dependent, so naturally I'm not super stoked on part of that RNG being me guessing what any given thing is ACTUALLY going to do. Lastly, there's so much wasted potential when it comes to making this game visually interesting, because right now IT IS NOT. I definitely recommend the devs play some Inscription and take notes. Then animate the interiors of the dice, they're currently so flat and uninteresting. You're leaving so much "OOOO SHINEY" dopamine on the table and it makes my inner crow very sad. I also recommend more interesting dice effects in general. But also LET ME START PICKING MY HAND WHILE THOSE ANIMATIONS PLAY. I'd rather have to change a few things than sit there while all the animations play out. Most runs aren't very animation heavy, but my first one ever absolutely was, and it was annoying. Just have stuff play out in the order of operations that are most likely to change a players decision. AKA spawn extra dice first, do extra damage last. I want to like this game, but I currently kinda doooooont. My opinion could easily be changed by some simple changes though. TL;DR This is a game about dice, and the dice dont even look very good????

A relatively simple but still fun and relaxing roguelike, perfect to wind down a bit after a long day. It's basically The Seventh Seal, but you're playing dice instead of chess. Don't expect the level of complexity and craziness of something like Balatro, it's smaller in scope. Still, you get four classes(so far), each with their own gimmick that makes them feel quite distinct. Each of them also has a bit of a backstory that you uncover as you play and conversate with Death, which is a nice detail that fleshes out the game quite a bit. My only criticism on this bit is that some references are a bit too on the nose(for me anyway) and the Adventurer is a bit too silly, especially considering the other characters have a more somber script that matches the tone set by the visuals and audio. The balance is a bit off, though. I've played a fair bit now, and with the recent update I went through Circle 4(the hardest difficulty) with all classes to get the new dice. With the Soldier(the starting class) it took me about 10 attempts to beat Death once. With the Healer, 2. With the other 2, just one. I'm pretty sure I've never lost a game with the Adventurer no matter how brain dead my relic/dice picks were. People may be frustrated with the game's difficulty while not being aware that the first class is just kind of underpowered, even though it's probably the most fun one due to actually needing to think about your moves a bit more. Overall, hearty recommend.

If you absolutely love deckbuilding, it's a recommend; otherwise, you can skip this one. Pros: Aesthetics Mechanics of adding dice/relics to your pool Cons: Slow, even on 2x speed Gets repetitive quickly Gameplay forces you into certain types of play depending on character choice, which isn't fun, especially for a roguelike. Too few dice/relics at the beginning Unlocking relics is more of a punishment than a reward From what I played, you can only have one die of each type, which means you can't truly customize to your heart's content Tried to ham-fist story into it, which overall felt weak to me. But the most egregious thing about the game: referring to a singular die as dice - every single time. How do you have a game about dice, and not know that the singular form of 'dice' is 'die' not 'a dice'. SMH. In all seriousness, the most egregious thing about the game is probably the fact that my second run was almost exactly like my first run because I hadn't unlocked many of the relics/special items yet. I truly find it unfun that a roguelike could have an almost exact replica of any run, much less your second. To get the same relics/dice and end up reconstructing my first deck was a hard no for me. I did keep playing, but once you start unlocking relics, you then dilute the pool of relics you can choose from. For example, there's a relic I really liked, but once I started adding more, I wasn't able to get that relic again - so unlocking relics felt more like a punishment than a reward. Then, once you start playing through various characters, you unlock THEIR special relics, which feel slightly stronger than the regular ones. I ended up feeling like I had to take my character's special relic, but then, again, I was just playing the same build over and over. I get that it probably sounds like I'm contradicting myself in the above paragraphs, but it's something I've seen being done in roguelikes more and more often. I like the way Hades and Dice and Pool did their relics, as compared to this game and Cult of the Lamb. I think it's because you get to choose which relics you play with at the beginning, as compared to then having a pool from which you select. It just hits different and not like you're being punished for playing the game. I also want to say having to sit through Death's rounds is very slow. It's not like you can avoid anything he does to you once he starts going, so I'm not sure why we can't have a skip button and just allow the punishment to come to us. In the later rounds, Death's turns can take a very long time. I thought about going and timing it, but then decided I'm just done with this game. But, without exaggeration, I'd wager Death's turns can take anywhere from 10-15 seconds, maybe even 20 seconds. It may not sound like a long time, but when you're just staring at dice flying into the air over and over, it can feel like an eternity. If anyone ends up timing Death's rounds, let me know. I'd be interested to know how close I was. Finally, I just want to add what's unlockable in this game is sort of.... unfun? It's just the same stuff you unlock during the main story, just for a different game mode. Very odd.

Vs death is fine, mostly, pinnacles are horrible, AI doesn't know how to play the builds it is playing, some matchups are impossible, with all the RNG you can get, with restarting until perfect start (because of 9000 IQ design decision to tie rerolling to a single item), every route available (around 90% items unlocked), which I have been doing for the past 6 hours (soldier 1 vs healer), cannot be done. I'm also 99% sure the rolls are not random, can't be bothered to write anecdotes but my pattern recognition is pretty solid at this point. There is also eternity or whatever it's called, which I never actually played, that should probably be the core infinite-loop mode, which I don't see a reason to play without everything unlocked, because of my past experiences of getting bent while my opponents pick a 3rd legendary dice out of their rectum in 6th round (pretty sure it's impossible for player to even find one in the pool that early), with every exact item to counter whatever I build, and that grind consists of beating either death or a matchup you know you'll win for like 50ish times, obviously not happening at this point. As it is now - nope.

It has the bones of a solid roguelike game. (pun intended) Rolling the virtual dice is enjoyable and the mechanics of dueling with dice is an interesting idea to me. I'm a fan of the pixel art, reading the conversations between rounds adds personality and history to each class. The difficulty is challenging, especially since I don't have much unlocked, but suppose that might be by design or due to RNG. I do like how you can gain new types of dice, relics, trinkets during a run, but I wish there were more possible upgrades e.g., leveling up types of scoring combinations, adding or removing pips in a die, maybe a way to disable/reroll one of death's bothersome relics, to feel like I have a bit more agency. I don't have many hours playing Dice With Death, however, it's a simple but enjoyable game, so I'll ROLL with that.

Likely not everyone's cup 'o tea but if you enjoy some roguelike deckbuilding elements layered on a bit of gambling, this'll be right up your alley.

Cleverly pushing the mechanical possibilities of Yahtzee, this tight little title offers a wealth of dice and relic combinations to spice up your Death-defying rounds.
A different take on Balatro + Yahtzee with a darker theme. This is not a strong recommendation; I'd give it a mixed review if possible. But it's worth checking out.
